_comment: Fixture: 2 candidates (1 Sonnet + 1 Opus), PASS on both post-verifications, first run. Exercises the happy-path end-to-end flow through Steps 1-11.
desired_outcome: A user who pastes a job description into the canvas system sees a structured BMC generated within 30 seconds, with all 9 blocks populated from the source text, and can export it as PDF.

candidates.design_context_override: favor explicit user gates over implicit automation

b1_output.agreed_solution_description: A FastAPI backend accepts a job description text, passes it to Claude Sonnet for structured extraction, and returns a populated BMC JSON. The React frontend renders the 9 BMC blocks from the JSON and offers a one-click PDF export via the browser's print API. The user pastes text, clicks Generate, waits up to 30 seconds, reviews the draft, and exports — three explicit gates, no hidden automation.

architecture_decisions.choice: Claude Sonnet with structured output tool-use
architecture_decisions.rationale: Sonnet balances cost and quality for the extraction task. Structured output guarantees the 9-block schema is always populated.
architecture_decisions.discovery_anchor: canvas system sees a structured BMC generated within 30 seconds

architecture_decisions.choice: PostgreSQL with a sessions table; no user auth in v1
architecture_decisions.rationale: Keeps state between Generate and Export without requiring a login flow. Sessions expire after 24 hours.
architecture_decisions.discovery_anchor: A user who pastes a job description

ux_decisions.choice: Single textarea with a Generate button
ux_decisions.rationale: Mirrors the user's mental model: paste text, click generate. No multi-step wizard.
ux_decisions.discovery_anchor: pastes a job description into the canvas system

abstraction_test.reasoning: Components named by role: ExtractionService, BMCRenderer, SessionStore. Each name conveys what it does to a domain reader.

responsibility_alignment_test.reasoning: ExtractionService owns text-to-BMC transformation only. BMCRenderer owns display only. No cross-cutting responsibility leakage.

evolution_test.notes: If the extraction model changes, only ExtractionService changes. If the BMC schema grows to 12 blocks, only BMCRenderer changes. Single-locus per change.

communications_patterns_test.notes: One-way flow: frontend → backend → Claude API → backend → frontend. No cycles.

data_connectedness_test.notes: Each component receives all data it needs from its upstream caller. No reaching out for state.

data_variations_test.notes: Empty textarea → disabled Generate button. API timeout → user-visible error with retry. Partial BMC → rendered with empty block placeholders.

discovery_anchors.excerpt: canvas system sees a structured BMC generated within 30 seconds
all 9 blocks populated from the source text

candidates.design_context_override: optimize for fewest moving parts — minimize new abstractions

b1_output.agreed_solution_description: A single FastAPI endpoint receives the job description, calls Claude Opus for extraction, and returns the populated BMC. The React frontend renders the 9 blocks and offers PDF export. No session storage — the frontend holds state in memory for the duration of the browser tab. Minimal surface area: one endpoint, one model call, one render component.

architecture_decisions.choice: Claude Opus with tool-use structured output
architecture_decisions.rationale: Opus is the most capable model for nuanced job-description parsing. The cost difference is acceptable at the expected usage volume.
architecture_decisions.discovery_anchor: all 9 blocks populated from the source text

architecture_decisions.choice: No server-side persistence in v1 — frontend memory only
architecture_decisions.rationale: Removes the sessions table, simplifies deployment, eliminates a failure mode. The user can re-generate if they close the tab.
architecture_decisions.discovery_anchor: A user who pastes a job description into the canvas system

ux_decisions.rationale: Zero additional backend work. Native browser feature. Works offline after generation.

abstraction_test.reasoning: Single endpoint and single render component — names ExtractionEndpoint and BMCView. Roles clear from names.

responsibility_alignment_test.reasoning: ExtractionEndpoint does extraction. BMCView does display and export. No overlap.

evolution_test.notes: If extraction model changes, one endpoint changes. If export mechanism changes (e.g. server-side PDF), one frontend component changes.

communications_patterns_test.notes: Frontend POSTs to endpoint, endpoint returns JSON. One round trip. No async messaging.

data_connectedness_test.notes: Endpoint receives all it needs from the POST body. View receives all it needs from the response JSON.

data_variations_test.notes: Empty input → validation error before API call. Timeout → error message. Partial extraction → rendered with explicit empty placeholders.

assumptions: Usage volume is low enough that Opus cost is acceptable in v1
